*Kusalattika, Cittaduka* (Patthana 16.16) is a textual section within the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and concluding treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. As designated by its title, the text structurally integrates the analytical categories of the *kusalattika* (the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states) with the *cittaduka* (the dyad relating to mind or consciousness), examining their conditional relations according to the twenty-four causal conditions (*paccaya*) typical of the *Paṭṭhāna* system [SuttaCentral].

Its most substantial formulaic overlaps occur with closely related sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1), *Kusalattika, Cittasaṁsaṭṭhaduka* (Patthana 16.19), *Mahantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.10), *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 10.1), and *Kusalattika, Cetasikaduka* (Patthana 16.17) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-level cross-language text alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā Lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093-2) [DharmaNexus].
